Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
955 PM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Some adjustments made to the fog potential for tonight, mostly
east of the Blue Ridge. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Cloudy finish to the weekend, with the potential for frost
  and freezing conditions west of the Blue Ridge by late Monday.

- 2) Dry conditions and warmer temperatures are forecast for
  Wednesday through Saturday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Cloudy finish to the weekend, with the potential
for frost and freezing conditions west of the Blue Ridge by late
Monday.

Latest guidance is quite bullish on fog development in a narrow
window tonight, between 05-10Z for areas east of the Blue Ridge.
This is before the main front arrives, which brings increasing
winds and drier air. The 00Z IAD sounding showed a saturated
boundary layer that is decoupled, so it is possible some fog
develops, but uncertainty remains how widespread it could be
given all the clouds. Maintained mostly patch fog, though some
areas of fog could develop.

Any residual cloud cover should erode as a cold front sweeps 
through the area early Monday morning. This yields a mostly 
sunny day with temperatures warming back into the upper 60s to 
mid 70s, with 60s across the mountains. Northwesterly winds pick
up behind the frontal system with afternoon gusts to around 20 
to 25 mph. A strong area of Canadian high pressure pushes in 
from the Midwest on Monday before settling over the local area 
by the overnight period. This sets the stages for the first 
widespread frost event, mainly west of the Blue Ridge. The 
Allegheny ridgetops could even near the freezing mark. For east 
of the Blue Ridge, forecast lows will be in the 40s.

High pressure maintains its influence over the area on Tuesday 
which brings cool temperatures, lighter winds, and sunny skies.
Most can expect highs in the 60s, with mid/upper 50s across
mountain locales. Tuesday night also looks chilly, but forecast
temperatures have come up a tad given light southerly flow
around the departing high pressure center. At this point
temperatures would be just mild enough to avoid another frost
event. For most, the forecast lows are in the low/mid 40s.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions and warmer temperatures are
forecast for Wednesday through Saturday.

High pressure will remain in control locally through much of the 
upcoming week. Dry conditions are forecast for Wednesday through 
Saturday, along with warmer temperatures. Highs each day will 
generally be in the 70s, with lows in the upper 40s to lower 50s.

There are signs that the stretch of dry weather will come to an end 
on Sunday as an area of low pressure tracks northward out of the 
Gulf toward the Ohio Valley. If this occurs, rain will likely move 
into the area from the south. However, there's still a lot of 
variability in model guidance with respect to what will occur with 
this system, and if/when we'll get rain.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
IFR ceilings will remain a fixture in the forecast for the 
remainder of the day and into the night. The CAD wedge maintains
its presence over the region with continued low stratus and 
prevailing north to northeasterly winds. Although some lingering
drizzle is possible this afternoon, the forecast does become 
drier. Restrictions should eventually lift just before daybreak 
on Monday as a cold front tracks through. Thereafter, VFR 
conditions are expected as Canadian high pressure moves in from 
the Midwest states. Northwesterly winds on Monday could gust up
to 20 to 25 knots, particularly during the afternoon hours. 
Winds eventually turn lighter and more variable on Tuesday with
high pressure in place.

VFR conditions are expected on both Wednesday and Thursday. 
Winds are forecast to be out of the south on Wednesday, and then
out of the west to northwest on Thursday.

&&

.MARINE...
North to northeasterly winds are currently gusting around 5 to
10 knots. Any increase in marine winds do not occur until the 
second half of Monday in response to a cold front. This boundary
crosses the waters Monday morning with a shift to mainly west 
to northwesterly flow. Gusts up to 20 knots are expected for 
Monday afternoon through much of the overnight hours. Small 
Craft Advisories are likely going to be needed across portions 
of the waters. Winds turn lighter into Tuesday with high 
pressure overhead.

Sub-SCA level winds are expected for both Wednesday and Thursday. 
Winds are forecast to be out of the south on Wednesday, and out of 
the west to northwest on Thursday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies have risen quite a bit over the last 24 hours 
with current values around 1 to 1.25 feet. This is bringing some
of the more sensitive locations into Action stage, with some
tidal flooding possible at Annapolis. The forecast ahead shows 
anomalies remaining elevated through tonight before post-frontal
northwesterlies begin to lower water levels a bit on Monday.

&&
